title: Synevid temporal journal envelope (Pillar 1)
description: The output document of `autopsy temporal`: the journal's own canonical projection, embedded verbatim under `journal`, plus the three facts the CLI adds about it. Closed: every field the engine can emit is declared and nothing else validates. The CLI wraps the projection in a named field rather than merging into it, so the array cannot be mistaken for the whole document and the engine's projection stays checkable as data.

journal.description: `TemporalJournal::to_canonical_json`, re-parsed: the facts the journal holds, in the engine's own order. Empty is a statement — the history it replays carries no facts — and is not the same statement as "the history is empty".

coverage.description: Derived from the fact counts: `unknown` facts make it `unknown`, `partial` facts make it `partial`, and only a journal whose facts all resolved is `verified`. Derived rather than asserted, because `--strict` must fail on precisely the facts the engine flagged.

notes.description: The CLI's own statements about the document, in prose — including the extractor's granularity (`TreeExtractor` records file presence per revision, not symbols), so the limitation travels with the machine-readable output and not only the text one.

active.description: Facts not retired at the head revision.

partial.description: Facts whose extraction could only resolve part of what it asserts.

fact.description: One claim about the repository at a revision, valid from the commit that introduced it until the commit that retired it. A fact is a *historical* statement: reviving a retired fact as a live edge is exactly what the temporal engine exists to prevent, so `valid_to` is part of the identity of an active-at-revision answer.

fact_id.description: BLAKE3 of `subject ‖ predicate ‖ object ‖ valid_from` joined with NUL separators.

subject.description: Canonical identity of the asserting entity.

object.description: Canonical identity of the asserted target, or an opaque value.

valid_from.description: Commit that introduced the assertion. A commit id, not a timestamp: the journal deliberately does not date a history, so nothing can be ordered by a clock that never entered the digest.

valid_to.description: Commit that retired the assertion, or `null` while it is active at the head revision.

evidence_digest.description: BLAKE3 of the content that proves this fact (AST slice or blob digest).
